question: A plane passes through the point $(2, -3, 1)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} - 5\hat{k}$. Write the equation of the plane in Cartesian form.
explanation:
The given vector $3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-5\hat{k}$ acts as the normal vector of the plane.

Using point-normal form: $A(x-x_1)+B(y-y_1)+C(z-z_1)=0$.

Substitute $(x_1,y_1,z_1)=(2,-3,1)$ and $(A,B,C)=(3,4,-5)$.

$3(x-2)+4(y+3)-5(z-1)=0$.

Simplifying gives $3x+4y-5z+11=0$.
